currentCard.prompt: Сколько пар черепных нервов выделяют в анатомии человека?

answers.note: Черепной нерв VIII — преддверно-улитковый; он относится к чувствительным нервам.
Черепной нерв X — блуждающий; он участвует в регуляции органов грудной и верхней брюшной полости.
Все двенадцать обозначаются римскими цифрами I–XII; блуждающий нерв X также связан с органами грудной и верхней брюшной полости.
Черепной нерв XI — добавочный; он контролирует мышцы шеи.

currentCard.explanation: В анатомии человека выделяют двенадцать пар черепных нервов, обозначаемых римскими цифрами I–XII. Они выполняют чувствительные, двигательные или смешанные функции.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e: 13.4 The Peripheral Nervous System

literal.prompt: Сколько пар черепных нервов выделяют в анатомии человека?

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: 13.4 L62 identifies twelve numbered cranial nerves I–XII; Table13.3 L81–L92 enumerates exactly those twelve named nerve classes. 16.3 L31/L34 independently state twelve, while bilateral examples (optic nerves on both sides L48 and hypoglossal nerves both sides L100) make clear this standard anatomical count is of named bilateral nerves/pairs, not 12 single unilateral trunks. Under conventional human I–XII classification, twelve pairs is the unique key; eight, ten and eleven are smaller totals. Four short count labels are comparable and grammatical.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: В анатомии человека выделяют двенадцать пар черепных нервов, обозначаемых римскими цифрами I–XII. Они выполняют чувствительные, двигательные или смешанные функции.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: 13.4 L62 supplies twelve and Roman numbering I–XII; L63/L75–L76 expressly classify nerves as sensory, motor or mixed. The two Russian sentences state those two supported facts, name the key and do not claim that every nerve has all three kinds of function.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Черепной нерв VIII — преддверно-улитковый; он относится к чувствительным нервам.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: 13.4 L75 explicitly maps eighth nerve to vestibulocochlear and purely sensory; Table13.3 L88 confirms VIII, name and sensory hearing/balance. 16.3 L38/L52 supplies the same mapping. The note is an explicit number-to-nerve association, not a claim that eight is the total count.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Черепной нерв X — блуждающий; он участвует в регуляции органов грудной и верхней брюшной полости.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: 13.4 Table13.3 L90 maps X to vagus and thoracic/upper abdominal visceral targets; L68/L71 describe homeostatic control. 16.3 L34 states cranial nerve X vagus has autonomic functions in those cavities. The note accurately relates number10 to a specific member and its function, not ten total pairs.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Все двенадцать обозначаются римскими цифрами I–XII; блуждающий нерв X также связан с органами грудной и верхней брюшной полости.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: 13.4 L62 supplies the group’s Roman labels I–XII, with all twelve rows in Table13.3; L68/L71/L90 locate vagus autonomic targets in thoracic and upper abdominal cavities. 16.3 L34 explicitly labels vagus X. Numbering adds a fact beyond total count; vagus is a specific member illustrating the numbered collection.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Черепной нерв XI — добавочный; он контролирует мышцы шеи.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: 13.4 L76 maps CNXI to spinal accessory, and Table13.3 L91 maps XI to motor head/neck and neck muscles. L68 directly states control of neck muscles. 16.3 L106–L109 details sternocleidomastoid/trapezius and head/neck movement, supporting the concise note without importing a new claim.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.prompt: Сколько пар черепных нервов выделяют в анатомии человека?
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.note: Черепной нерв VIII — преддверно-улитковый; он относится к чувствительным нервам.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.grammar: «Сколько пар…? — Восемь» is a correct cardinal-number answer, with «пар» supplied by the prompt, like the other three answers.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.plausibility: Eight is a plausible smaller anatomical count for a non-specialist and also a valid nerve index. It is a short numeric alternative with no syntactic/length clue.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.truthUniqueKey: The I–XII list has twelve named bilateral cranial nerve classes, not eight. Having an VIII nerve is not evidence for eight total pairs; the note explicitly calls it «нерв VIII», preserving index/count distinction.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.noteTruthUsefulness: VIII is exactly the Roman representation of this answer’s number8; teaching which cranial nerve bears that number and its sensory class is a concrete own-number association within this numbered set. It is useful positive information, not an unrelated nerve chosen arbitrarily, and makes no false eight-pair assertion.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.prompt: Сколько пар черепных нервов выделяют в анатомии человека?
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.note: Черепной нерв X — блуждающий; он участвует в регуляции органов грудной и верхней брюшной полости.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.grammar: «Десять» completes the same count question grammatically and its note is a well-formed sentence with the named nerve as subject.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.plausibility: Ten is a plausible nearby count and a real cranial nerve index; it is neither absurd nor marked by wording.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.truthUniqueKey: 13.4 L62 and complete table continue through XI and XII, so ten cannot be total number of conventional pairs. X denotes vagus, a numbered member, not all members.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.noteTruthUsefulness: The note explicitly links this option10 with nerveX, names vagus, and teaches its thoracic/upper abdominal regulation. That exact numeral-to-member relation makes the own-option connection substantive while keeping ordinal label distinct from total count.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.prompt: Сколько пар черепных нервов выделяют в анатомии человека?
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.note: Все двенадцать обозначаются римскими цифрами I–XII; блуждающий нерв X также связан с органами грудной и верхней брюшной полости.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.grammar: «Двенадцать» is the same cardinal answer form as the three distractors. The note’s «Все двенадцать» refers to the twelve named nerve pairs/classes and its following clauses are coherent.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.plausibility: A familiar anatomy fact can be recognised by the thematic audience, while uninformed players face four realistic counts of the same entity. No answer-form cue singles out12.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.truthUniqueKey: Both primary chapters state12; 13.4 explicitly numbers I–XII and lists all twelve. Bilateral examples in16.3 establish how named nerves occur on both sides. Thus key2 follows the standard classification independently of frozen key metadata.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.noteTruthUsefulness: Roman nomenclature I–XII is not supplied in prompt/key, so it adds a useful fact about the entire correct twelve-member series. The vagusX visceral territory is also a true fact about a member of that series; repetition with note10 or explanation is not a prohibited cross-note duplication.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.prompt: Сколько пар черепных нервов выделяют в анатомии человека?
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.note: Черепной нерв XI — добавочный; он контролирует мышцы шеи.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.grammar: «Одиннадцать» is a correct count-form answer; «добавочный» is used as an established nerve name with an explicit neck-muscle function in its note.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.plausibility: Eleven is a close neighbouring number below twelve and a genuine cranial nerve index, giving a credible mistake to someone with partial knowledge.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.truthUniqueKey: The numbered list includes XII beyond XI; 13.4 L62/Table13.3 show twelve, so eleven is not the complete pair count. XI is accessory, not a statement of total cardinality.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.noteTruthUsefulness: The note positively identifies nerveXI as accessory and its neck motor role. It teaches a checkable association specific to this answer11 rather than generic nervous-system text, and the explicit XI index prevents reading it as a claim of eleven pairs.

absoluteLevel.individualGround: Twelve pairs is a standard introductory human-anatomy fact known to people familiar with the nervous system; unlike everyday organ recognition it is not reliably broad adult knowledge. An uninformed player must choose among plausible counts8/10/12/11 with no textual cue. The question asks no individual nerve nucleus, specialist exam or obscure exception, so MEDIUM is appropriate rather than EASY or professional-detail HARD.

correctNoteExtraFact.fact: The twelve cranial nerve pairs/classes are designated by Roman numerals I–XII.
correctNoteExtraFact.beyondPromptAndKey: Prompt/key supply only the cardinal total, not the naming system or Roman notation. Thus the first clause already adds an own-group fact. VagusX thoracic/upper abdominal targets add a concrete member example, and overlap with explanation or distractor10 note is allowed.
